hook: You know the saying that money is the root of all evil. But did you know 1 Timothy 6:10 says something else?
known: Often remembered as the saying that money is the root of all evil.
audience: Timothy, with instructions he is to pass on to the church.
setting: A passage about contentment: “godliness with contentment is great gain”, and “having food and clothing, we will be content with that”.
around: The verse itself reads: “the love of money is a root of all kinds of evil”. The verse before it is aimed at “those who are determined to be rich”.
point: Three small words change the saying. The problem named is the love of money, and not money. It is a root, and not the only one. And it leads to all kinds of evil, which is not the same as every evil there is. The warning is about what a person wants most.
story:
Timothy opened this letter in Ephesus, a city that knew exactly what happens when faith threatens income.

Acts tells the story. A silversmith named Demetrius made his living from silver shrines of the goddess Artemis. When Paul’s preaching began to hurt the trade, he called the craftsmen together and started with the plain truth: “Sirs, you know that by this business we have our wealth.” Soon the whole city was in uproar, and a furious crowd poured into the theater shouting the name of their goddess.

So when Paul warns Timothy about the love of money, he is not being abstract. He had lived through what it could do to a city. And he gives Timothy a different kind of wealth to want: “godliness with contentment is great gain”.
